### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, traces split after A21 into two mutually exclusive branches: about 52 in 100 cases ran A21 → A22 → A23, while the other about 48 in 100 ran A21, then all three of A27, A28 and A33, then A23. A22 never co-occurred with any of A27, A28, A33, and A21 and A23 were present in every trace of both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL001, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR001, POS001]

- Within the block branch, the three activities always ran as a complete set of three (each pair co-occurred in about 48–49 in 100 traces) but in no fixed order among themselves — each ordered pair appears in both directions at roughly 24–25 in 100 block cases. [REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

- In the later window, virtually all traces (199 of 200) follow A21 → A22 → A23: A22's participation rose from about 52% to about 99.5% (still at most once per trace), and A21's outgoing transitions concentrated on A22 (about 52% before versus about 99.5% after, with the earlier shares to A27, A28 and A33 of roughly 14–18% each gone). [OCC001, REL001, REL005, DIR001, LAG001]

- A27, A28 and A33 each fell from about 48–49 in 100 traces to 1 in 200; the single later trace containing them contains all three. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL012, REL013, REL014]

- The A21→A23 distance changed accordingly: before, A23 followed A21 two positions later in about 52% of traces (via A22) and four positions later in about 48% (via the block); in the later window the two-position gap covers about 99.5% of traces, and A23's relative position moved slightly earlier (mean about 0.55 to about 0.53), consistent with the shorter path. [LAG001, POS001]

- The later outgoing-transition and distance profiles of A27, A28 and A33 each rest on that one trace and carry little weight on their own. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the alternative branch formed by A27, A28 and A33 between A21 and A23 is no longer executed, so that A22 has effectively become a mandatory step between A21 and A23. In the earlier window the two branches were taken in roughly equal shares (about 52 versus 48 in 100 cases); in the later window the block branch appears in only 1 of 200 traces, while A21 → A22 → A23 runs in essentially every trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL001, REL005, REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR001, LAG001]

Supporting signs: 34 control-flow items qualified against about 0.45 expected without change, far beyond what random re-splits produce; participation, routing, co-occurrence/order and distance indicators all show the same difference directly, and the key items are computed over all 200 traces per window rather than rare variants. [OCC001, DIR001, REL001, LAG001]

Limitations: most items describe the same trace-level difference and are not independent confirmations; and because the block still occurs in one later trace, the evidence cannot distinguish a branch that was removed from one that remains executable but is now chosen very rarely — the block's internal later behaviour rests entirely on that single trace. [REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

Other differences: none beyond the main hypothesis; the slight forward shift of A23's relative position is a consequence of the block dropping out rather than an independent change. [POS001]
